content.title: About
content.content: Cauliflower is a cruciferous vegetable related to broccoli and Brussels sprouts. When quickly cooked in a small amount of oil it stays crisp and develops a mild nutty flavor. It is low‑calorie and packed with nutrients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name “cauliflower” comes from the Latin *caulis* (stem) and *flos* (flower), although the vegetable can be white, green, purple or orange.
It was first domesticated in the Mediterranean region more than 7,000 years ago.
Vitamin C is better retained with short‑heat methods such as sautéing.
Cauliflower contains glucosinolates that may support the body’s detox pathways.
In Japan, cauliflower is often used in tempura, where it is briefly deep‑fried in a light batter.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is important for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Good source of fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: A serving of sautéed cauliflower provides about 70–90 kcal, making it diet‑friendly.

items.title: Provides antioxidants
items.content: Compounds like glucosinolates help combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Cruciferous allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience an allergic reaction to cauliflower.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: High intake of oxalates can contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible individuals.

items.title: Added fat during cooking
items.content: Using too much oil can increase the calorie count of the dish.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sautéed cauliflower works as a side dish, can be tossed into salads, pastas, grain bowls, or used in vegetarian tacos. Choose oils with a high smoke point such as olive or canola oil.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh cauliflower in the refrigerator’s vegetable drawer, loosely wrapped in a perforated bag, for up to 5 days. Cooked sautéed cauliflower should be consumed within 2–3 days and stored in an airtight container in the fridge.
